And that is the overcapacity bus management policies in Canadians' cities. And I'll turn it over to General Manager, Terry Schmidt. Thank you, Madam Chair. Terry Schmidt, General Manager of Transportation and Construction. This report provides information on how other Canadians' cities handle overcapacity buses and if they have policies for managing overcapacity buses. The report also provides information on work underway at Saskatoon Transit to provide real time information to riders on routes with capacity issues.

Saskatoon Transit invited Canadian Urban Transit Association or QDA agencies across Canada to complete a benchmark survey to understand of full buses or experience in other municipalities and how the agencies monitor and manage the issue.

Fifteen transit agencies responded and the results are summarized in an appendix one. Like most agencies respond into the benchmark survey, Saskatoon Transit does not have a formal policy to manage full buses.
It responds to capacity concerns by adding an extra bus or increasing the frequency of trips on a busy route when an issue persists and buses are available.
Currently, the limited fleet size and number of buses available for service prevent Saskatoon Transit from using these common strategies to respond to all known capacity issues.
Rights and bus assignments are planned using population and neighborhood growth trends and enrollment forecasts from high schools and post-secondary institutions.
Based on bus availability, permanent service changes are implemented each summer we're needed or throughout the year on a case by case basis.
Operators track instances of full buses manually and the ridership data will become increasingly more accurate as automated passenger counter APCs are installed on more buses.

The processes and procedures Saskatoon Transit uses to manage over capacity buses aligned with industry best practices and general processes and procedures in place at other Canadian cities that responded to the benchmark survey.
Twenty three buses in the Saskatoon Transit fleet currently have APCs installed and all new buses are ordered with APCs.
Additionally, a tender to retrofit a further 50 buses recently closed and with the eight new buses on order this will bring the total number of buses of the APCs to 81 by late fall.
Digital service alerts push to customers through the Transit app and posted to the Saskatoon Transit website and third party trip planning apps have proven to be successful communications tool.
Keeping customers informed in real time of service impacts such as detours, stop closures, delays and service cuts.
Integrations with vehicle monitoring systems have improved the consistency and quality of these alerts.

As more information is it becomes available from ABC's Saskatoon Transit will determine the feasibility of providing full bus information to customers in real time with push notifications through the Transit app and posted to the Saskatoon Transit website and third party planning apps.
This would complement the current use of full bus head signs on buses to communicate full buses.

Saskatoon Transit launched a comprehensive communications planning mid-August to assist riders in preparing for the full buses expected to start this week when high school and post secondary classes resume.
This is in addition to separate communications plan for the start of free fare for children starting September one.
That started on September one and the ongoing frontline employee safety plan.
Saskatoon Transit will continue to monitor instances of over-capacity buses and pass-ups using current processes and procedures engage with its key stakeholders and adjust service where possible.

Through integrations with vehicle monitoring systems, Saskatoon Transit will also continue to investigate and implement service alert improvements and determine the feasibility of providing full bus information to customers in real time using information from the ABC's.

The eight new buses arriving in the fall of 2024 and the 20 new buses arriving in late 2025 will allow Saskatoon Transit to better manage overcrowding on busy routes following the processes and procedures currently in place.
